liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): Reviewer says it went badly: tempo too slow, Garcia's leads incoherent, and Phil seemed out of tune; Bobby tells the band to hammer in time during this song; reviewer unsure whether aimed at Jerry or Keith [8][12][15]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Jerry and Donna sing well here, and it ends with a high-energy guitar solo [14]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer says the Not Fade Away into Black Peter segment is very hot [11]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer lists the Playing jam among the show's highlights [11]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 other source): Listed as the encore [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Poacher Story**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-07.sbd.miller.83715.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 172 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording quality great; Reviewer says the sound is great; This soundboard has very little stereo separation [1][14][15]
- **gd1978-04-07.164367.sbd.stereo.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 21 songs; 179 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1978-04-07.150559.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 178 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd78-04-07.sbd.connor.10208.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 172 min; rated 2.57/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound is excellent, and the 7-inch two-track reel source beats the cassette masters; Sound quality is very good despite the weak performance; Reviewer calls the sound quality terrific, though the show itself felt weird [7][8][10][12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer claims Garcia was using white powder, the band was sleepless, and the crowd was full of bikers on downers [9]
- Reviewer felt the band was out of sync all night, with heads not in it, though sound quality is very good [8]
- Reviewer hears a sloppy, slow, hazy show, exhausted and uncohesive, with Jerry off [12]
- Reviewer hears a spacey, tired, 'Sunday morning coming down' feel throughout, heard via XM radio [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-07.sbd.miller.83715.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) D [1]. Also: Chain is Sony 54P to cassette master to MiniMe to Samplitude; A Playing In The Band section (7:15-7:39) is patched from a source recorded by Robert Wagner [1]
- **gd1978-04-07.164367.sbd.stereo.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 11, 2023; source: SBD > Master Reel (7in 7.5ips 1/2trk) > PCM > DAT (44.1k) [2]. Also: This is the only circulating stereo source; others are the right channel split into two channels; Patch source was recorded by Robert Wagner [2]
- **gd1978-04-07.150559.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by PCM Source & Transfer by Anonymous Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel August 14, 2020; source: Betty Cantor’s Master SBD Reel > PCM > PCM [3]. Also: This Betty Board transfer was shared by an anonymous person, with a patch from Bob Wagner (Charlie Miller) [3]
- **gd78-04-07.sbd.connor.10208.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Reviewer notes this circulating version comes from a 7-inch two-track reel rather than a cassette master; Reviewer's soundboard copy came from taper/trader cmiller; Source is a 7-inch two-track reel at 7.5 ips, through a PCM501ES to DAT, then Wavelab editing [4][7][11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1978-04-07 Fri Sportatorium, Pembroke Pines, FL](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1479395591103/grateful-dead-1978-04-07-fri) [20]
